$comment: THE LEDGER (ARCHITECTURE.md §1, I-10).
Every tuned constant, with the artifact that justifies it.
A constant not in this ledger may not steer behavior.
Two sections, because there are two kinds of constant and only one of them is in the
engine:
constants           — constants in the ENGINE. Still empty: nothing is tuned yet. There
is no cache, no batch size, no threshold, and no benchmark. The
first entries arrive when the first constant does (RocksDB block
cache and bloom filters in C8, consolidate() tuning in C10), and
each arrives with its receipt or not at all.
generator_constants — constants in the SCENARIO GENERATOR. These do not steer the engine;
they steer what the test suite covers, which deserves a receipt at
least as much. An engine constant set badly makes the engine slow.
A generator constant set badly makes a green suite meaningless —
and it does so silently, because everything still passes.
An entry has the shape:
"name":        "the constant, as it appears in code",
"value":        <the value>,
"location":     "path.rs",
"steers":       "what this changes",
"justification":"why this value and not another, in terms of a measured number",
"artifact":     "testing/evidence/<file> — committed, regenerable, checked by a test",
"measured_on":  "the machine and configuration, or 'deterministic' when the
measurement is a pure function of its inputs and has no machine",
"sprint":       "CN"

generator_constants.name: KEY_DOMAIN
generator_constants.steers: The range of values in the `id` column, which is the column every generated join joins on.
generator_constants.justification: The join-key domain sets how often two tables share a key at all. Measured at the committed artifact: of 371 join-family scenarios where both tables ended up populated, 251 produced a non-empty bare join. Before narrowing the domain the same measurement read 69 of 141 — under half — so most join scenarios were comparing two empty answers, which agree no matter how broken either side is. Three values is the smallest domain that still lets a null key, a matching key, and a non-matching key all occur.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: operation weighting
generator_constants.steers: Whether tables accumulate rows over a scenario or hover near empty.
generator_constants.justification: With insertions and retractions balanced, a table stays near empty: joins find nothing, groups hold one row, and the suite spends its epochs comparing empty answers. Insertions outnumber retractions 3:2 so tables grow. Retractions remain a quarter of all operations outright, and update and churn carry negative weights too — measured at the artifact, 808 of 1,000 scenarios contain a retraction and 377 contain one in epoch one. The §6 C0 bar is that retractions are present from epoch one; this raises coverage without lowering that bar.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: operations per table per epoch
generator_constants.steers: How much each non-empty epoch changes.
generator_constants.justification: The lower bound was 0, which allowed a scenario to seal eight epochs and still hold no data. A run over an empty table proves nothing about a join or an aggregate. At least one operation per table per non-empty epoch guarantees the scenario is about something.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: empty-epoch rate
generator_constants.steers: How often a sealed epoch carries no changes at all.
generator_constants.justification: §7 requires empty epochs: the answer must not move across one. Measured at the artifact, 647 of 1,000 scenarios contain at least one, which is ample for `an_empty_epoch_never_changes_the_answer` to have something to check in every family.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: empty-input rate
generator_constants.steers: How often a whole scenario carries no data at all.
generator_constants.justification: §7 requires empty inputs — an engine that is wrong on an empty input is wrong before it starts. Measured at the artifact, 150 of 1,000. Higher would waste the sweep on the least informative case; zero would drop a case §7 names.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: predicate depth and connective weighting
generator_constants.value: depth 1 (depth 2 one time in four); OR twice as likely as AND, NOT least likely
generator_constants.steers: How selective a generated WHERE clause is.
generator_constants.justification: Each level of AND roughly halves the rows that survive, and a filter admitting nothing turns the scenario into an expensive way of comparing two empty answers. Nesting still occurs; it is not the default shape.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: comparison operator weighting
generator_constants.steers: How many rows a generated comparison admits.
generator_constants.justification: Over a domain of a handful of values, `= literal` admits roughly one row in six while `<= literal` admits about half. Equality is kept because joins and group keys need it, but weighting toward the inequalities keeps answers non-empty often enough to be worth comparing.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: typed-NULL comparison rate
generator_constants.steers: How often a comparison is against a typed NULL, making the whole predicate NULL.
generator_constants.justification: Comparing to NULL makes the predicate admit nothing (S-13), so as a top-level filter it empties the scenario. It is generated because 'neither matches nor complements' (S-17) is real behaviour worth covering, but rarely, because every occurrence costs a scenario.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: column-divisor rate
generator_constants.value: 2/3 of generated divisions divide by a column rather than a non-zero literal
generator_constants.steers: How often a generated expression can raise DivisionByZero (S-21).
generator_constants.justification: Until C3 the generator never raised, because the oracle and the engine disagreed about what an error meant to a standing query and both gates had to assert that none occurred. D-16 settled that (an error is a property of the contents, S-22), so raising expressions belong in the population. Measured at the regenerated artifact: 14 of 1,000 scenarios raise, across 35 comparisons, and both implementations agreed at every one. The rate is set by how often arithmetic appears at all rather than by this knob — raising the column-divisor rate from 1/3 to 5/6 moved the scenario count only from 14 to 15 — so it sits at a middle value and the specific error behaviours are pinned by handwritten scenarios instead.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: extreme integer literal rate
generator_constants.steers: Whether +, -, * and SUM can overflow (S-20, S-30).
generator_constants.justification: One kind of live error would never exercise S-22c's rule that the least message wins when several are live. An occasional i64::MAX literal gives a second kind — ArithmeticOverflow and AggregateOverflow alongside DivisionByZero — without touching the column value domain, which stays small so that collisions remain likely.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads

generator_constants.name: null rate in generated values
generator_constants.steers: How much three-valued logic the scenarios exercise.
generator_constants.justification: Nulls are the common case in this dialect, not the exception (S-13…S-18): they change comparison, grouping, aggregation, and joins, each differently. A quarter is frequent enough that every null-sensitive rule is hit across a sweep, without making the data mostly absent.
generator_constants.measured_on: deterministic — a pure function of the seed range, no timing and no threads
